subject: URGENT: Hydra SDK chunk alignment regression causing P99 spikes
messages:
From: Eli Torres <eli.torres@hydra-payments.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 and dropped frames on live ingest

Marissa —

We started seeing big P99 latency spikes on our live ingest at 07:48 PDT and then intermittent dropped frames across several lanes. Our SREs captured a few client-side PCAPs and some application logs (attached). The errors look like parser failures inside the Redwood client SDK where header boundaries are misaligned: some frames are merged and others split incorrectly. This started after the SDK update you shipped on Monday (v1.4.7).

This is impacting checkout throughput (we're seeing ~25% drop in effective TPS). Can you confirm if this is a known regression and whether you can provide a rollback or patch? We need an ETA — this is on our incident commander's critical list.

Thanks,
Eli
Lead SRE, Hydra Payments

Attachments: hydra-ingest-logs-20260611.tar.gz, sdk-pcap-sample-01.txt

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Eli Torres <eli.torres@hydra-payments.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:28:12 -0700
Subject: Re: High p99 and dropped frames on live ingest

Eli —

Thanks for the quick heads up and for attaching the logs. Sean and Jonas are awake and triaging now. Initial ask: can you confirm which client language and which exact SDK artifact SHA you upgraded to (npm/yarn/GH release)? That will help us narrow whether this is a packaging/regression or a runtime interaction with your ingress proxies.

We will start with a quick rollback plan if we identify v1.4.7 as the culprit. I'll keep you posted every 30 minutes while we triage.

- Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:03:45 -0700
Subject: RE: High p99 and dropped frames on live ingest

Quick triage notes:
- Replayed the PCAP Eli sent in a staging harness. Parser state machine mis-identified header delimiter when a trailing CRLF is split across packets. The SDK merge routine then concatenates chunks without re-running delimiter detection, which can yield a malformed header block for the downstream parser.
- Repro is highest at ~10k rps and with TLS segmentation similar to their frontend. Lower QPS hides it.
- Hypothesis: a change in the chunk coalescing path in v1.4.7 removed a safety check introduced in 1.4.4.

Action items (my notes):
1) Roll back Hydra to SDK v1.4.6 in canary for their ingestion cluster (if they can) — this avoids the new coalescer.
2) Patch: reintroduce delimiter re-validation before header parse (fast patch, low-risk).
3) Longer: add fuzzing harness and an integration test that simulates split-delimiter TCP segmentation.

I'm spinning up a repro cluster and a minimal fix branch. Will update with a build in ~45m.

- Sean

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:05:02 -0700
Subject: RE: High p99 and dropped frames on live ingest

Marissa/Team —

We should escalate to execs now because Hydra is a strategic mid-market customer in renewals and this is affecting checkout. Recommendation: loop in Sales Head and the CTO for a rapid credit/compensation decision and to ensure legal is ready if the degradation hits SLAs.

Prepared blurb for execs (short):
- Impact: Hydra Payments experiencing ~25% TPS reduction and intermittent client-side parsing errors after Redwood SDK v1.4.7. Root cause likely regression in chunk coalescing logic causing header delimiter misalignment under TLS segmentation.
- Mitigation in flight: immediate rollback to v1.4.6 in customer canary + fast patch branch to re-run delimiter check. ETA for patch build: ~2 hours; hotfix rollout: ~4 hours pending validation.
- Ask: decision on one-time service credit and a committed follow-up date for a formal RCA and test-suite additions.

If you approve, I'll send the note to Sales Head and CTO and ask for a 1pm call.

- Jonas

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, cto@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:22:10 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Hydra Payments — live ingest parse regression impacting checkout throughput

Hi Rishi / Vivek / CTO —

Summary: Hydra Payments (key renewals customer) is reporting a production regression after upgrading to Redwood client SDK v1.4.7. Symptoms: P99 latency spikes and dropped frames leading to ~25% throughput loss. Engineering triage indicates a regression in the SDK chunk coalescer that can misalign header delimiters under typical TLS segmentation patterns.

Mitigations in flight:
- Canary rollback to v1.4.6 (customer-side) — in progress; asking Hydra to flip canary ASAP.
- Fast patch branch to re-run delimiter validation before header parsing; build & unit tests targeted in 2 hours.
- Validation plan: synthetic high-QPS replay + Hydra staging harness.

Requested executive decisions:
1) Approve an immediate one-time service credit up to 10% for the impacted billing period if rollback fails.
2) Approve a 1pm incident call with Hydra leadership (their execs are available).
3) Prioritize the parser-fuzzing integration story in the next sprint for a higher test bar.

Attachments: summary timeline and the Hydra logs (see Drive).

Will wait for guidance.

Thanks,
Marissa
